title: Ember shift — handoff fragments and quick fixes
body:
EMBER SHIFT HANDOFF — freeform notes (Sofia M.)
Shift window: 19:00 — 03:00 PT 

Quick summary:
- Quiet first half-hour. Small spike at ~19:42 (p95 token latency bumped from 160ms -> 420ms for hosted-api route /v1/generate).
- Cause: short-lived thrash when a dedicated pool entered maintenance and routing fell back to smaller quantized variant. Automated fallback worked but increased latency.
- Resolved by scaling up dedicated pool (see commands below) and reverting aggressive routing rule I added earlier (rule: prefer-quant-small when load>75%).

Live / active items (please pick up):
1) INF-4271 — intermittent model OOMs on dedicated-pool-east-2 (older GPUs). Seen 3x this week. Next action: schedule a maintenance window with infra to upgrade driver stack or pin those customers to quantized 8-bit variants instead of full fp16.
2) Flight of new batcher config (experiment-B) — still in canary: look for increased tail latencies in requests where seq_len>2048. If p99 > 1s for 5m, rollback to experiment-A.
3) Alerts: 'kv-cache-stale' fired twice at 02:11. Investigate next shift — likely GC marker interaction with cache coordinator.

Recent deploys / context:
- 2026-03-11 18:40 — routing: add-pref-quant-small rule (temporary) — reverted at 20:05 when fallbacks caused p95 spike.
- 2026-03-09 03:20 — batcher: experiment-B rollout 10% traffic to canary nodes in dedicated pools.
- Note: customer-redwood-inc had a dedicated capacity change at 19:00 (auto-burst) — correlated with the fallback event.

Checks to run at start of shift (copy/paste):
- Check service health dashboard: Console > Routes > Hosted API > /v1/generate (time window 30m).
- kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving --selector=app=router -o wide
- kubectl logs -n redwood-serving <router-pod> -c router --tail=200 | grep "fallback=" | tail -n 80
- Check dedicated pool utilization: curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_CLI" https://infra.internal.redwood/pools | jq '.[] | select(.name=="dedicated-east-2")'

Quick troubleshooting snippets collected (handy):
- Force a routing switch back to baseline: POST /internal/routing/set?policy=baseline (requires infra token).
- Scale dedicated pool: infra-cli pools scale --pool dedicated-east-2 --replicas 6  # current 4 -> 6
- Restart cache coordinator: kubectl rollout restart deployment/cache-coordinator -n redwood-cache
- Check KV cache health: curl -s http://cache-coordinator.internal/health | jq .status   ("ok" expected)

Temporary mitigation I used tonight (notes):
- Reverted pref-quant-small rule via internal routing API (saved p95 but increased cost for a bit).
- Temporarily added a short-lived autoscale override to dedicated-east-2 (+2 replicas) to smooth the tail. Keep this if we see another fallback in the next hour.

Open questions / TODOs for next shift:
- Confirm whether driver-510.* stack upgrade eliminated OOMs on older GPUs. I left a note in INF-4271 for infra to follow up.
- Decide on long-term policy for routing when pools enter maintenance: prefer fallbacks + shed load gracefully OR pre-warm smaller variants? Pros/cons documented in Confluence link but needs product sign-off.
- Find owner to trim stale canary Batcher configs — experiment-B has no owner listed in the docs (tagging @Arjun in Slack).

Escalation contacts (in order):
- On-call SRE (primary): Arjun Patel — slack @arjun (work: +1-415-555-0131)
- Infra SME: Maya Rivera — slack @maya (work: +1-415-555-0199)
- Product emergencies: Priya Desai — slack @priya-p (pager for P0)

Commander notes for next on-call (short, actionable):
- If you see p99 token latency > 1s for > 5m across multiple routes, do NOT immediately increase batch sizes. First: check for routing fallbacks and dedicated pool scaling. Increasing batch size when fallback is in effect makes the tail worse.
- If you see repeated `model_oom` errors from the runtime, attempt a canary restart of the affected node group; if OOM persists, mark nodes as unschedulable and file INF-4271.

Ad-hoc observations (scratch):
- Alerts noise: `kv-cache-stale` seems to correlate with small GC spikes on coordinator (rare 1-2s pauses). Consider moving coordinator to converged nodes with fewer tenants.
- Customer report: support ticket RDW-804 flagged degraded embeddings on a private deployment; looks like a misconfigured batcher parameter on their private instance. Sent links to solutions-eng.

Snippets / commands log (what I ran during shift) — copy/paste friendly:
- infra-cli pools list --region east-2 --format table
- infra-cli pools scale --pool dedicated-east-2 --replicas 6 --reason "ember-shift emergency scale"
- POST /internal/routing/set?policy=baseline  (curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $INF_TOKEN" ... )
- kubectl logs -n redwood-serving router-0 -c router --tail=500 | grep fallback

Notes to self (less formal):
- Remember to clean up the autoscale override in the morning (I left a TODO comment in the infra ticket).
- Param names are inconsistent across docs: batcher_timeout vs batch_timeout — file a tiny doc-update PR.

Wrap-up for sign-off at end of shift:
- Double-check that the reverted routing rule stayed reverted (I put a sticky note in Slack: #oncall-ember pinned message).
- Remove the +2 replica override if p95 returns to baseline for > 20m.
- Add a short entry to Confluence with timeline of the fallback event (I started a stub page: Confluence: internal/postmortems/ember-fallback-2026-03-11).

If you pick this up: ping me in Slack (Sofia M.) if you need context; I left comments on INF-4271 and OPS-1198 with the debugging commands I used.

-- end of fragment --

(These are my personal handoff fragments — meant to be ephemeral. When things get stable, move action items into the team runbook in Confluence.)
